_comment: H-1B petitions approved and denied by employer, USCIS Employer Data Hub, FY2009-2023. INITIAL AND CONTINUING ARE KEPT APART: an initial approval is a new worker entering the programme, a continuing approval an extension or amendment for someone already in it, so summing them counts the same person across years. Headline figures use INITIAL approvals. DENIAL RATES ARE A POLICY SERIES -- they move with adjudication policy rather than with applicants, and a change says more about the agency than about employers. Counts are PETITIONS, not people. Employers are grouped on the filed name with case and whitespace normalised only; nothing is fuzzy-matched, so two spellings of one company remain two rows and a company total is a FLOOR -- materially so: Cognizant files under five spellings whose combined initial approvals are more than twice its largest single one. The name_variants block lists each spelling with its own count so the addition is visible rather than assumed. USCIS also ships rows with no employer name; those are counted in the national totals and reported as blank_employer_rows.
